ETHICS production annotation analysis

Verified input and protocol

The supplied production exports contain 9,975 instructions, not 9,875: 1,995 in each of the five partitions. There are 29,925 human ratings from 19 annotators, exactly three distinct annotators per instruction. All 9,975 reconstructed human majorities match archive A's export; all 9,975 reconstructed rationale records match its rationale aggregate. This run consumes A's normalized individual exports; it does not rerun normalization of the 95 original macro-enabled workbooks.

Archive B supplies 9 model conditions and 89,752 rows. There are 23 absent rows, 2 empty final labels, and 27 invalid final labels. Every present row is aligned to the human data using partition plus an explicit instruction ID or metadata ID, and its normalized scenario text is verified. No rows are joined by position or fuzzy text similarity. Model identifiers below are read from the archive, not independently verified release descriptions.

The production protocol, not the preliminary 500-item protocol, governs the analysis: commonsense principles apply to both judgments; deontology principles apply only to MORALLY RIGHT/WRONG main rationales; justice is single-choice; utilitarianism now has ten structured multi-select rationale categories; virtue free text is required only for YES. Inapplicable rationales are not missing data. Numerical rubric references and exact category names followed by definitions are normalized with an audit trail. Unrecognized text is never converted to OTHER.

Overall chance-adjusted values are weighted means of within-partition coefficients, not coefficients calculated by treating different domain labels as the same category. Human-majority agreement is a study-reference concordance measure, not a moral-correctness measure. The leave-one-out file evaluates held-out humans against the other two raters only when those two agree; it never evaluates a human against a majority containing their own vote. It is not an ethical ceiling.

These are available-case results. judgments/model_vs_human.csv additionally supplies common_all comparisons using the exact common valid item set for all nine models, and common_frontier comparisons for the three-model frontier panel. It reports coverage, confusion matrices, balanced accuracy, macro-F1, MCC, reference prevalence, agreement with the full human vote distribution, and lower/upper agreement bounds for missing or invalid labels. Overall balanced accuracy, macro-F1, MCC, and κ are valid-item-weighted domain means. Use judgments/paired_model_comparisons.csv for paired differences on identical items: exact McNemar tests in item-bootstrap mode, stratified paired-bootstrap intervals, and Holm adjustment across all model-pair/domain tests. In cluster-bootstrap mode, item-independent McNemar p-values are suppressed.

judgments/item_consensus.csv includes each instruction's label votes, strict majority or tie, valid-panel size, unanimity among available responses, complete-panel unanimity, mean pairwise agreement, entropy in bits, and relation to the human majority. Group Fleiss κ uses complete panels; nominal Krippendorff α uses all items with at least two valid ratings. The overall Fleiss denominator may therefore differ from the overall raw-agreement denominator. Ensemble majority labels abstain on ties and require at least two valid votes. Vote entropy is panel disagreement, not calibrated model uncertainty.

Rationale agreement and ethical attention

All model-human rationale references retain only human annotators whose binary label matches the human majority: two humans for split items and three for unanimous items, before field eligibility checks. The primary majority_aligned scope does not require the model's label to match.

For the same-judgment analysis, a model must agree with the human-majority judgment; only eligible human rationale annotations carrying that same final judgment enter its reference. Both actors therefore express the same judgment before their rationale distributions are compared. The primary human reference is item-balanced: average eligible human category vectors within each item, then sum over the same paired items as the model. Annotation-pooled versions reproduce the earlier response-pooling convention as a sensitivity analysis.

The displayed extrema describe actor-specific eligible cohorts and are not paired superiority tests. rationales/paired_rationale_distance_contrasts.csv recomputes selected model-pair TV differences on an identical eligible cohort and identical bootstrap draws. All rationale intervals are descriptive, pointwise 95% intervals, not multiplicity-adjusted confirmatory tests.

For multi-select fields, mention shares sum to one and support total variation (TV), Jensen–Shannon divergence in bits, and entropy. Selection prevalence is the fraction of eligible responses selecting each category; its sum may exceed one. Both are exported, but TV is never misapplied to unnormalized prevalence vectors. Fractional-response profiles and cardinality statistics show whether apparent profile differences are driven by selecting more categories per response.

Itemwise overlap averages Jaccard, Dice, and exact-set match over valid model–human pairs within an item, then averages across items. Empty/inapplicable sets never manufacture perfect agreement. Single-choice fields additionally have weighted nominal κ; category-level binary κ exposes the influence of nonselection. Human and model internal rationale baselines are provided separately. Internal human reliability and raw field-quality diagnostics retain all original individual annotations; they are not majority-filtered reference measures. These are properties of expressed categories, not evidence about internal causal reasoning.

The detailed log distinguishes absent rows, invalid labels, unrecognized categories, unfilled templates, missing eligible rationales, and extra inapplicable rationales. Legitimate justice OTHER choices remain distinct from invalid final-label OTHER. The old pilot's GaMS justice parsing exclusion is not imported into the new dataset: quality decisions are based on the present files.

Investigation and descriptive analyses

review/all_items_with_evidence.csv joins every scenario, human vote/rationale evidence, model judgments/rationales, and transparent review flags. priority_review.csv and first_100_review_cases.csv focus on coverage issues, unanimous model–human disagreements, human ambiguity flags, and low rationale overlap despite matching judgments. Flags prioritize human inspection; they do not automatically label either side as erroneous.

Source train/test, human unanimity, ambiguity flags, and culture-reference flags are reported in judgments/stratified_model_vs_human.csv. These are descriptive strata; unflagged does not mean culturally neutral, and the ETHICS source split is not evidence of model-pretraining separation. Virtue YES-rationale lengths and repetition are analyzed descriptively, without inventing a semantic similarity score. Logged frontier token/cost totals concern supplied returned rows only, not failed requests, retries, or complete experiment expenditure.

Reproducibility and inference scope

This run used 5,000 percentile bootstrap resamples, seed 20260917, sampling instructions within ethical partitions and preserving the complete human/model bundle for each selected instruction. The same bootstrap weights support paired comparisons. Input hashes, software versions, configuration, timing, source-code hashes, and detailed denominator/status exports accompany the results.

The bootstrap is conditional on these annotated items and this fixed annotator/model pool. It does not quantify variation across new human populations, model reruns, temperatures, or prompts. Potential dependence among related source scenarios should be assessed with the optional cluster-map bootstrap rather than claiming universal independent sampling. No API requests are made.

Principal files

audit/audit_summary.json, audit/coverage.csv: counts, reconciliation, and missingness.

judgments/model_vs_human.csv: per-model, per-partition, overall, and common-item results.

judgments/item_consensus.csv: every instruction's model consensus.

judgments/pairwise_model_agreement.csv, group_reliability.csv: model–model agreement.

judgments/paired_model_comparisons.csv: paired statistical comparisons.

rationales/model_human_distances.csv, paired_category_profiles.csv: ethical-attention distributions.

rationales/model_human_overlap.csv, item_model_human_overlap.csv: active-set and same-judgment overlap.

rationales/field_quality.csv: eligibility-aware rationale quality.

review/priority_review.csv: auditable disagreement cases with source text.

Methodological continuity

The supplied preliminary papers motivate separating final-judgment agreement from expressed moral grounds, preserving individual human rationale choices, using active-set overlap for multi-select fields, and using paired item bootstraps for distributional distances. Their older model releases, 500-item sample, and older utilitarianism rationale format are not substituted for the present production data.
